title: Energy Emergency Leadership Act
official_title: To amend the Department of Energy Organization Act with respect to functions assigned to Assistant Secretaries, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Introduced by Rep. Laurel M. Lee (R-FL) and passed the House by voice vote (no recorded roll call); the bill assigns energy emergency and security functions to an Assistant Secretary at the Department of Energy and now awaits Senate consideration.
summary: Adds energy emergency and energy security duties to the list of functions the Secretary of Energy may assign to an Assistant Secretary. These duties cover energy infrastructure security, cybersecurity, and helping state, local, and Tribal governments respond to energy threats when they ask.
brief: Assigns energy emergency and energy security functions to an Assistant Secretary at the Department of Energy.

top_lines.headline: Energy Emergency and Security Functions
subs: Adds a new function class to Assistant Secretary duties under the DOE Organization Act
Covers infrastructure security, resilience, emerging threats, cybersecurity, and supply
Includes emergency planning, preparedness, coordination, response, and restoration

top_lines.headline: Technical Assistance to Governments
subs: Provides technical assistance on request of a State, local, or Tribal government
Also available on request of an energy sector entity
Aims to protect against, detect, and respond to energy security threats and incidents

top_lines.headline: Interagency Coordination
subs: Secretary must ensure the new functions are performed with relevant Federal agencies

items.main: Names the Act the "Energy Emergency Leadership Act".
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Functions Assigned to Assistant Secretaries

items.main: Amends subsection (a) of section 203 of the Department of Energy Organization Act (42 U.S.C. 7133(a)) to add a new paragraph (12) listing energy emergency and energy security functions among those assigned to Assistant Secretaries.
items.detail: The new functions include responsibilities for energy infrastructure, security and resilience, emerging threats, cybersecurity, supply, and emergency planning and preparedness, coordination, response, and restoration, as appropriate.

items.main: The new paragraph authorizes, upon request of a State, local, or Tribal government or energy sector entity, the provision of technical assistance and support to protect against, detect, and respond to energy security threats, risks, and incidents.
items.detail: Such assistance is to be provided in coordination with other Federal agencies as appropriate. It is triggered by a request from the covered government or energy sector entity rather than initiated unilaterally.

items.main: Directs the Secretary of Energy to ensure the functions described in the new section 203(a)(12) are performed in coordination with relevant Federal agencies.
items.detail: This coordination requirement applies to the functions added by this Act. The bill states no funding, deadline, or reporting requirement for the new functions.

underreported.section: Section 203(a)(12)(B) — technical assistance to energy sector entities
underreported.summary: Beyond governments, the new paragraph lets the Department provide technical assistance and support to an "energy sector entity" upon its request to protect against, detect, and respond to energy security threats.
underreported.why_unreported: The short title frames the change as internal leadership on energy emergencies, but the operative text extends Department technical support directly to private energy sector entities on request.

gaps: The bill assigns energy emergency and energy security functions but does not appropriate any funds or specify staffing for carrying them out.
The bill authorizes technical assistance upon request but sets no deadline, standard, or eligibility criteria for responding to such requests.
The bill directs coordination with relevant Federal agencies but does not name the agencies or specify how coordination is to occur.

added: New paragraph (12) in section 203(a) of the Department of Energy Organization Act listing energy emergency and energy security functions
New authority to provide technical assistance and support to State, local, or Tribal governments and energy sector entities upon request
modified: Amends subsection (a) of section 203 of the Department of Energy Organization Act (42 U.S.C. 7133(a)) by adding the new function class at the end

featured_quotes.name: Ms. Lee
featured_quotes.text: This legislation passed out of the Subcommittee on Energy unanimously because both Republicans and Democrats on the Committee recognized how critical it is to have accountable leadership protecting our electric grid. Today, the United States is experiencing record energy demand, driven by artificial intelligence, data centers, renewed domestic manufacturing, and widespread electrification across our economy. Meeting that demand safely requires not only robust and reliable generation but also a secure and resilient grid to deliver it.
